title: Finite reductions of a derived-complete constructible complex
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal. On the small pro-étale and étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-site] use constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $N\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\underline A)$ be locally derived $J\underline A$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Suppose $N\otimes_A^L\underline{A/J}\simeq
u_X^*C$, where $
u_X$ is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $C$ is a bounded étale $A/J$-complex, and each $H^q(C)$ has a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which it is locally constant with finitely generated $A/J$-module values [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose integers $a\leq b$ satisfy $H^q(C\otimes_{\underline{A/J}}^L F)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $A/J$-module sheaf $F$ and every $q
otin[a,b]$.

Put $N_n=N\otimes_A^L\underline{A/J^n}$, with the quotient transitions. Then $N\simeq R\varprojlim_nN_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit], $H^q(N)=0$ for $q
otin[a,b]$, and each $N_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on the pro-étale site. There are bounded étale $A/J^n$-complexes $C_n$ with constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, isomorphisms $\alpha_n:
u_X^*C_n\simeq N_n$, and isomorphisms $ eta_n:C_{n+1}\otimes_{\underline{A/J^{n+1}}}^L\underline{A/J^n}\simeq C_n$. One may choose $C_1=C$ and the given residue isomorphism. The $ eta_n$ satisfy the quotient cocycle, and $\alpha_n
u_X^* eta_n=ho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^L\underline{A/J^n})$, where $ho_n$ is the canonical tensor-associativity normalization of the reduction tower. No quotient $A/J^n$ is assumed finite or perfect over $A$.

proof.text: The finite affine cover makes $X$ quasi-compact: restrict an open cover to each affine, choose finite subcovers, and take their finite union, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It is locally Noetherian by the stipulated affine-cover definition, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Every $P_n=A/J^n$ is Noetherian: inverse images of its ideals are finitely generated ideals of $A$, and their generators descend. Thus the comparison theorems below apply to $X$ and to each discrete coefficient ring $P_n$.

source.place: Tag 09C2 setup; Tag 01OY (locally Noetherian implies quasi-separated)

proof.text: Choose one K-flat resolution $P\to N$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The complexes $P\otimes_A P_n$ represent $N_n$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and are K-flat with flat terms over $P_n$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Consequently, for every degree-zero $P_n$-module sheaf $F$, $N_n\otimes^L_{P_n}F$ is represented by $(P\otimes_A P_n)\otimes_{P_n}F=P\otimes_AF$. For $m\ge n$, balancing gives $\rho_{m,n}:N_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n\simeq N_n$, represented by $(p\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto p\otimes q_{m,n}(u)v$, with inverse $p\otimes v\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes v$. For $r\ge m\ge n$ both iterated maps send $((p\otimes u)\otimes v)\otimes w$ to $p\otimes q_{r,n}(u)q_{m,n}(v)w$; thus these normalizations satisfy the quotient cocycle and commute with maps of representatives.

source.place: Tag 09C2 quotient reductions; K-flat change of rings and explicit tensor balancing

proof.text: The assumed Tor tests say exactly that $C$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on the étale site. The given constructible cohomology and boundedness put $C$ in $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},P_1)$. By [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian], $N_1\simeq\nu_X^*C$ has the same Tor interval on the pro-étale site. The constructible comparison [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] also makes its cohomology constructible. Exactness of comparison inverse image [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves] identifies its cohomology with the pullbacks of those of $C$.

Fix $n$ and any degree-zero $P_n$-module sheaf $F$. Its finite filtration $F\supset JF\supset\cdots\supset J^nF=0$ has quotients $G_i=J^iF/J^{i+1}F$ annihilated by $J$. By Step 2, $N_n\otimes^L_{P_n}G_i=N_1\otimes^L_{P_1}G_i$, which has no cohomology outside $[a,b]$ by Step 3. Tensoring the short exact sequences of this filtration with $P$ remains termwise exact since its terms are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Their long exact cohomology sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], inducting up from $J^nF=0$, therefore give the same vanishing for $N_n\otimes^L_{P_n}F$. This proves the required Tor amplitude for every $n$ by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]; taking $F=P_n$ also proves that $N_n$ itself is supported in $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 0942 (sites-cohomology-lemma-bounded), proof of (2), finite ideal filtration

proof.text: The given local derived $J\underline A$-completeness is precisely the complete-subcategory condition in [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. Its completion adjunction identifies the unit on a complete object with an isomorphism, so $N\simeq R\varprojlim_nN_n$. To retain the upper endpoint $b$, tensor $0\to J^n/J^{n+1}\to P_{n+1}\to P_n\to0$ with the flat-term complex $P$. The first resulting complex is $N_1\otimes^L_{P_1}\underline{J^n/J^{n+1}}$ by Step 2 and has Tor-test cohomology in $[a,b]$. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] gives an epimorphism $H^b(N_{n+1})\to H^b(N_n)$. Work throughout over the common sheaf $\underline A$, forgetting the quotient scalar actions. Write $\mathcal M=\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\underline A)$. Its countable products are exact by [det-pe-products-exact]; it is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] therefore identifies the K-injective strict-tower limit in the completion formula with a derived limit in the Roos-triangle sense. For the strict representatives $T_n=P\otimes_A P_n$ from Step 2, [det-pe-products-derived] identifies their termwise product $V=\prod_nT_n$ with the product in $D(\mathcal M)$. The chain map $1-T:V\to V$ satisfies $\mathrm{pr}_n(1-T)=\mathrm{pr}_n-t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, where $t_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n$ is induced by the quotient. Rotating the cone triangle in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] makes $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$ another derived limit of this same tower. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] supplies an isomorphism between these two limit objects; only the cohomology bounds, not a canonical comparison map, are needed here. Now [det-pe-milnor-sequence] gives $0\to R^1\!\varprojlim H^{q-1}(N_n)\to H^q(N)\to\varprojlim H^q(N_n)\to0$. Outside $[a,b]$ both end terms are zero, except potentially the left term for $q=b+1$; that term is zero by [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] and the epimorphisms just proved. Hence $H^q(N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.

proof.text: Constructibility in [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] is local on $X$, so Step 3 supplies, for each of the finitely many degrees $a\le q\le b$, an open covering of $X$ on whose members $H^q(N_1)$ has a finite stratification. Intersecting members of these finitely many coverings gives one open covering of $X$ by opens $U$ on which every $H^q(N_1)$, $a\le q\le b$, has a finite stratification. Restriction to $U$ along the open immersion is the exact pro-étale restriction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and commutes with the reductions by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and constructibility of $N_n$ is checked on such $U$; so fix one $U$ and write $X$ for it in the rest of this step (only the scheme structure of $X$ and of its affine opens is used below). Refine the finitely many stratifications of $H^q(N_1)$, $a\le q\le b$, as follows. For each tuple of input strata take their finite fibre product over $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and omit the empty products. This is the scheme-theoretic intersection with its actual projection morphisms to all input strata. Indeed write each input immersion as closed in an open neighborhood [def-weil-closed-immersion]; on the intersection of these open neighborhoods and on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R$ therein, the product is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I_1\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_RR/I_s)=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(I_1+\cdots+I_s))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The ring equality follows from $1\otimes\cdots\otimes1\mapsto1$ and the quotient maps as mutual inverses, so these products are closed in that open intersection. Their images are the finite intersections of the input subsets, hence pairwise disjoint and covering $X$. For a projection $h:T\to S$ to an input stratum, pull its pro-étale trivializing covering $\{V_i\to S\}$ back by the covering-preserving base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The inverse image preserves finite limits and all colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. It therefore preserves constant sheaves: the constant set sheaf with value $M$ is the coproduct of $M$ copies of the terminal sheaf (maps into any sheaf are $M$-indexed global sections); naturality in $M$ preserves the ring and module operations. Its constant-ring isomorphism agrees with $c^h_{P_1}$ because both are adjoint to the same constant sections. On $T\times_S V_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] identifies the restriction of $h^*$ with the inverse image of the localized morphism; the same constant-sheaf argument applies there. Thus each pulled-back covering trivializes the restriction by the same finite-type module. The adjoint-compatible composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] identifies the iterated restrictions with restriction along the actual composite immersion. Thus the resulting finite stratification makes every cohomology sheaf of $N_1$ locally constant of finite type. Fix one such stratum $i:S\to X$ and $n\ge1$. Exact pro-étale restriction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the derived tensor pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify $(N_n|_S)\otimes^L_{P_n}P_1$ with $N_1|_S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-reduction-lissity] on $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with coefficient ring $B=P_n$, ideal $I=J/J^n$, and complex $K=N_n|_S$. Here $K$ is bounded above by Step 4, $B$ is Noetherian by Step 1, and $I^n=0$. Its final clause therefore makes every $H^q(N_n|_S)$ locally constant of finite type over $P_n$. This proves constructibility of all the reductions on that finite stratification. No finiteness of the underlying sets of $P_n$ is used.

source.place: Tag 09C2 proof of (3); Tag 09BR (lemma-compare-truncations-constructible), realized stratumwise by Tag 094I

proof.text: For each $n\ge2$, Steps 4 and 6 put $N_n$ in the bounded constructible pro-étale category for $P_n$. The equivalence [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] gives $C_n\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},P_n)$ and $\alpha_n:\nu_X^*C_n\simeq N_n$. Use $C_1=C$ and the prescribed isomorphism for $\alpha_1$. The reverse implication of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] puts every $C_n$ in the same Tor interval $[a,b]$. This uses each ring $P_n$ separately, never a finite-ring or perfect-$A$-module identification.

For $m\ge n$, put $Q_{m,n}=C_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n$ on the étale site. It has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$: for every $P_n$-module sheaf $F$, a flat-term K-flat representative $R\to C_m$ gives the chain isomorphism $(R\otimes_{P_m}P_n)\otimes_{P_n}F\to R\otimes_{P_m}F$, $(r\otimes v)\otimes f\mapsto r\otimes vf$, with inverse $r\otimes f\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes f$, identifying $Q_{m,n}\otimes^L_{P_n}F$ with $C_m\otimes^L_{P_m}F$, which has the required vanishing by Step 7. In particular $Q_{m,n}$ is bounded. It also has constructible cohomology. Indeed, as in Step 6, pass to an open covering of $X$ on whose members the finitely many nonzero $H^q(C_m)$ all have finite stratifications (étale restriction to an open is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and commutes with the reduction by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]), and on each member apply the explicit fibre-product refinement construction of Step 6 to these finite stratifications, obtaining actual projection morphisms to the input strata. The étale coverings pull back to coverings by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]; the localization and constant-sheaf argument of Step 6 applies to the étale inverse image as well, using the inverse-image adjunction in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Exact étale restriction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and tensor pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] reduce to each stratum; there [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor] applies to $C_m$ and the constant finite-type $P_m$-module $P_n$ in degree zero, both bounded above. It gives locally constant finite-type cohomology. The resulting local trivializations, initially $P_m$-linear, are $P_n$-linear because the scalar action factors through $P_m\twoheadrightarrow P_n$; their model modules are finitely generated over $P_n$ by the same generators. Thus $Q_{m,n}\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},P_n)$.

Derived tensor pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the constant-coefficient identification in [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves] identify $
u_X^*Q_{m,n}$ with $
u_X^*C_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n$. Therefore $\alpha_n^{-1}ho_{m,n}(\alpha_m\otimes^LP_n)$ is an isomorphism $
u_X^*Q_{m,n}	o
u_X^*C_n$. Both its source and target are in the bounded constructible comparison domain by Steps 7 and 8. Full faithfulness of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] lifts it uniquely to $ eta_{m,n}:Q_{m,n}	o C_n$; lifting its inverse shows that this is an isomorphism. Taking $m=n+1$ gives the required $ eta_n$ and, by their definition, the stated compatibility equation with $\alpha_n$ and $ho_n=ho_{n+1,n}$.

source.place: Tag 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived); explicit full-faithfulness transport of the quotient normalization

proof.text: For $r\ge m\ge n$, compare $\beta_{r,n}$ with $\beta_{m,n}\circ(\beta_{r,m}\otimes^LP_n)$ under canonical tensor balancing. Apply $\nu_X^*$ and then $\alpha_n$. By Step 9 the latter composite becomes $\rho_{m,n}\circ(\rho_{r,m}\otimes^LP_n)\circ(\alpha_r\otimes^LP_n)$: the intervening $\alpha_m^{-1}$ and $\alpha_m$ cancel. Step 2 identifies this with $\rho_{r,n}\circ(\alpha_r\otimes^LP_n)$, the image of the former map. Faithfulness of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] gives equality. For $m=n$, Step 2 gives the unit normalization $\rho_{n,n}$; hence the compared map is $\alpha_n^{-1}\rho_{n,n}(\alpha_n\otimes^LP_n)$, which is the unit map $C_n\otimes^L_{P_n}P_n\to C_n$. Faithfulness gives this identity normalization for $\beta_{n,n}$. This proves the quotient cocycle, retaining exactly the original $C_1$ and residue marking chosen in Step 7.

split_report.summary: Replaced the earlier three proposed children by existing general interfaces. The proof now carries the finite-filtration Tor argument, the quotient-tower normalizations on a single K-flat representative, the top-degree epimorphism and Milnor bound, stratumwise nilpotent constructibility, and the unique full-faithfulness lifts with explicit cocycle cancellation. The statement and all arbitrary Noetherian coefficient hypotheses are retained. No new nodes are needed. Second reading explicitly connected the K-injective completion limit to the Milnor cone via exact products, enough injectives, derived products and the derived-limit comparison; cited the existing long exact cohomology interface and expanded quotient balancing and identity normalization. Second reading also made the common-stratum construction explicit as fibre products, with affine ideal sums and actual projections, and reused it in Step 8. A further source check supplies the localization, covering and composition interfaces for pulling local trivializations to common strata.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the ancestor det-lem-integral-models-stacks proof residue/Tor clause and the integral-models unit proof (3) invocation of Stacks 09C2; no chapter or unit route changed.
